sentences.text: This animal belongs to the group of armored dinosaurs known as ankylosaurids.
It was a medium-sized creature that grew to be between four and five meters long.
The animal walked on four legs and lived on the ground while eating plants.
Small, polygonal bone plates were located on the skull just behind the eye socket.
The original name came from damage to the fossil that took away the teeth.
Sternberg thought the missing teeth were actually crushing plates because of the compression.
Charles Mortram Sternberg gave the genus its name in the year 1928.
He based this naming on the holotype specimen identified as CMN 8530.
The skeleton was gathered by Sternberg in 1916 from a quarry near Morrin.
The specific name lambei was chosen to honor the Canadian geologist Lawrence Morris Lambe.
A study in 1986 showed that specimen AMNH 5266 belonged to a young Anodontosaurus.
That same specimen was found in 1912 along the Red Deer River by Barnum Brown.
Victoria Arbour suggested the genus is different from Euoplocephalus based on skull features.
She also pointed out differences in the rings on the neck and the shape of the tail club.
This dinosaur is placed within the subfamily Euoplocephalini.
It is classified inside the larger family Ankylosauridae.
The animal is a member of the bird-hipped dinosaur class Ornithischia.
Victoria Arbour and Philip Currie formally revalidated the genus in later work.
A specimen from the Dinosaur Park Formation was later set as the holotype for a new species.
The species Anodontosaurus inceptus is a subdivision described by Penkalski in 2018.
Arbour argued in 2010 that the genus was valid after re-describing Dyoplosaurus.
Another specimen from the Dinosaur Park Formation, TMP 1997.132.1, was moved to this genus.
That Dinosaur Park specimen was eventually named the holotype for the new species A. inceptus.
The time range for this animal spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian.
Fossils were found in the upper part of the Horse Canyon Formation dating from 71 to 70.2 million years ago.
The scientific validity of the genus was formalized through three separate studies.
